entry.summary: Revising the sampling protocol after the pilot workshop. A second crew will try the draft sequence during a practice collection.
items: A cross-team review identified two ambiguous collection steps.
The revised procedure is being checked by field and data staff.

entry.summary: Presented the pilot at the regional research conference. Attendees asked how the pilot results could be reproduced from the sample files.
items: The session included a short live demonstration.
Questions focused on reproducibility and data access.

entry.summary: Host a tour of the visualization space for visiting collaborators. The visit will include a short explanation of the synthetic input data.
items: Confirm accessibility needs and visitor names.

entry.summary: Published a curated test dataset with a versioned data dictionary. The release includes units, missing-value codes, and a note identifying all sample values as synthetic.
items: The release contains 240 synthetic observations.
Checksums and a reuse note accompany the files.

entry.summary: Submitted a follow-on proposal for instrument time and analyst support. The submission includes a range for instrument use and the analyst time needed to review each run.
items: The proposal requests two experimental campaigns.

entry.summary: Presented the first simulation results and the uncertainty bounds. The group recorded which assumptions needed a clearer caption before sharing the figures.
items: The baseline case stayed within the expected range.
A sensitivity run showed the largest change under delayed restoration.

entry.summary: Install the replacement gateway at the western monitoring station. The installer will check the first packet and record the restart sequence.
New team members are completing instrument safety training. The supervisor will confirm each person can complete the preparation checklist.
items: Two people completed the online module.
The supervised laboratory session is scheduled next week.

entry.summary: Coordinating a working session with utility analysts and researchers. The group is collecting questions to resolve before the next simulation review.
items: The team is drafting shared assumptions.
The agenda includes a review of data provenance.

entry.summary: Released parser v2.1 for the telemetry stream, including a retry path for partial uploads. The team checked that a partial transfer can be retried without introducing duplicate measurements.
items: Automated checks cover missing and duplicated packets.

entry.summary: A methods preprint was indexed for the pilot study. The team checked the title and version against the published record.
items: The record points to the openly available manuscript.

entry.summary: Run hands-on training for new model reviewers. Each reviewer will record the steps needed to reproduce the figure.
items: Participants will reproduce a short synthetic scenario.

entry.summary: Confirmed the data handling designation for this synthetic demonstration. The decision is recorded with the release notes for future reviewers.
items: The sample has no sensitive source records.

entry.summary: Archived the first-cycle retrospective after actions were transferred to the project plan. Its decision log links each open question to an owner and the evidence expected at the next review.
items: A replacement data review step is now tracked by the project lead.

entry.summary: Released the scenario viewer with clearer legends and keyboard navigation. Reviewers can compare scenarios without relying on color alone to identify the selected region.
items: The release includes a compact layout for print review.
The 24-hour chart labels were checked at 100% scale.
A CSV export supports follow-up analysis.

entry.summary:
Validated the October sensor inventory against the deployment register.

The inventory now separates active devices from equipment retained for comparison runs. Reviewers can trace every plotted series back to a station without relying on informal naming conventions.
items: The review identified two retired station identifiers.
A corrected mapping is included in the synthetic data package.

entry.summary:
Screened a small synthetic materials library for stable candidate compositions.

The screen uses the same input assumptions for every candidate and records why a composition was excluded. The resulting list is a starting point for discussion, not a claim that any material has been validated.
items: The initial screen narrowed the list to twelve candidates.
No experimental claim is made from this fixture data.

entry.summary: Reviewing input tables for missing values and inconsistent time zones. Analysts are keeping a list of fields that need a documented correction.
items: The synthetic load table uses hourly UTC timestamps.
A sample report explains how blank readings are treated.
Reviewers will sign off on the revised dictionary.

entry.summary: Replaced the enclosure gasket at the north-bank monitoring station. The repair was completed before the next scheduled collection window. The team recorded the seal material and inspection date so later moisture readings can be interpreted with the maintenance history in view.
items: The enclosure passed a controlled spray test.

entry.summary: Refining the sample preparation sequence to reduce variation between batches. Operators reported that two preparation steps were described in different places. The revised sequence brings them together and adds a pause to confirm the instrument state before measurement begins.
items: The draft sequence specifies timing and temperature checks.

entry.summary: Checked the demonstration workstation and display capacity before the next review. The team also rehearsed switching between scenarios while the secondary display was connected.
items: The workstation completed the sample scenario without interruption.
The shared display remained readable from the back of the review room.
Keyboard and pointer controls were available for the same workflow.

entry.summary: Drafted a common checklist for field crews collecting calibration samples. Field staff asked for a shorter sequence that can be followed while wearing gloves. The revision keeps the measurements in a fixed order and reserves a place for observations that do not fit a predefined code.
items: The checklist records instrument firmware and reference conditions.
A trial run will test whether the instructions are clear in poor weather.

entry.summary: Reconciled specimen labels between the microscopy and spectroscopy tables. The mismatches came from abbreviated labels in one export format. A crosswalk is now kept with the tables so later analyses do not silently combine different specimens.
items: Three label mismatches were corrected in the test copy.

entry.summary:
Assembled a synthetic set of hourly demand traces for the demonstration.

The traces include predictable daily variation and a few controlled disruptions to exercise the charts. They are labeled synthetic throughout the report so readers do not infer real operating conditions.
items: The traces cover weekday and weekend patterns.
All values are fictional and intended for layout testing.

entry.summary:
Added a visible warning when telemetry packets arrive outside the expected time window.

Delayed packets previously appeared as current observations in the overview. The new warning makes the delay visible without discarding the original timestamp or changing the stored measurement.
items: The warning includes the station identifier and the observed delay.

The release check followed a delayed packet from the device archive through ingestion, storage, dashboard display, and CSV export. Reviewers compared the packet timestamp with the receipt timestamp at each step and confirmed that the warning stayed attached to the observation when filters changed. They then repeated the check with a current packet to verify that ordinary readings were unaffected. The test record includes the station name, expected label, actual label, and a screenshot of the warning at high text scaling. The checklist will be reused after the next parser release to confirm that the same behavior persists.

entry.summary:
Released a preview notebook that plots composition against measured response.

The notebook keeps data loading, calculations, and chart construction in separate cells. A reviewer can rerun the example and see how a changed threshold affects the plotted comparison.
items: The notebook includes a reproducible environment file.

The review run starts from a clean environment, loads a small synthetic specimen table, applies the documented preprocessing rule, and regenerates every figure in the notebook. A second analyst compares the table values with the plotted points and checks that the legend still identifies the correct sample group after changing a threshold. The exported image, table, environment information, and run date are kept together under one example identifier. If a result differs, the analyst records the exact cell and input that changed rather than treating the notebook as a single opaque output. The team also checks the output at larger text scaling and in a grayscale printout so the example remains interpretable in the PDF appendix.

entry.summary: Documented the assumptions used by the baseline restoration scenario. The note explains which loads may be restored together and where the model applies a simplifying limit. It gives reviewers a way to challenge assumptions without first reading the simulation code.
items: The method note names the decision points that users can vary.

entry.summary: Held a joint review of collection priorities with the university field team. The discussion also identified a mismatch in how the two teams describe sampling locations. A shared location table is being prepared before the next coordinated visit.
items: The teams agreed to sample the same three tributaries during the next visit.

entry.summary: Coordinating a shared measurement plan with an external instrument team. The plan identifies measurements needed for the pilot decision and those that would only be useful in a larger study. That distinction should keep the first transfer small enough to inspect manually.
items: The teams are aligning sample identifiers and file naming before transfer.

entry.summary: Improving keyboard navigation in the scenario comparison panel. The team is testing the panel with only a keyboard and at higher text scaling. Findings are recorded by task so a visual fix does not obscure a navigation problem.
items: The next review will test focus order and visible focus indicators.

entry.summary:
Comparing bank-side and midstream readings to estimate local mixing effects. The comparison uses matching time windows and excludes samples taken during equipment maintenance. Results will remain labeled provisional until the team can repeat the analysis under higher flows.

For the next pass, analysts will align the readings by station and flag intervals with incomplete coverage. The comparison table retains the excluded records and the reason for each exclusion, so a reviewer can distinguish a data quality decision from an environmental effect.
items: Early plots show that the difference varies with flow rate.
The analysis remains provisional until the next sampling round.

entry.summary:
Prepare the methods appendix for an open review draft. The appendix will describe instrument settings, normalization, and the reason particular records were set aside. It will also identify which numbers are synthetic examples in the review draft.

A short worked example will follow one specimen from raw observation through normalization to the reported value. The example is small enough to audit by hand and identifies each choice that could change the comparison. Reviewers will be able to distinguish a measurement result from a value included only to illustrate the calculation.
items: The appendix will describe quality controls and excluded measurements.

entry.summary:
Compared restoration outcomes under two alternate crew availability assumptions.

Both assumptions were applied to the same scenario set. The comparison highlights where staffing changes the timing of recovery and where network constraints remain the dominant factor.
items: The direction of the main result remained unchanged.

entry.summary:
Updated the demonstration schedule after the field vehicle became unavailable.

This change affects transport and staffing but not the planned review criteria. The schedule records who will collect replacement observations if another visit is lost.

The revised calendar preserves the original collection targets alongside the new visit dates. This lets the field lead see where a missed visit changes seasonal coverage and where an existing sample can still support the planned comparison.
items: The revised plan keeps the data quality review on its original date.

entry.summary:
Verified the calibration state of the pilot characterization instrument.

The calibration review found no issue that would block the fixture demonstration. Its record includes the check date and reference condition so the screenshots have credible context.

The instrument log and image capture settings are linked to the same demonstration identifier. This allows the team to update a screenshot later without losing the calibration context that was present when the example was first assembled.
items: The check used a synthetic control sample for this layout fixture.

entry.summary: Prepare a second display station for the group demonstration. The second station will mirror the primary display but use a simplified control surface. This allows visitors to follow the comparison while a presenter changes the main scenario.
items: The station will use a larger monitor for side-by-side review.

entry.summary:
Published a sample metadata table with units and missing-value codes. The table is intended to travel with exported data rather than remain in a separate note. Reviewers can use it to distinguish a true zero from an unavailable observation.

The release notes define each field in the table and include a small worked example of an absent value. A downstream analyst can use the example to verify that their import script has not converted missing observations into measured zeroes.
items: Each variable has a plain-language definition for reviewers.

entry.summary:
Onboarded a new analyst to the pilot data review process. The onboarding exercise exposed an instruction that assumed prior knowledge of the specimen codes. The team is rewriting that step before the next analyst repeats the exercise.

The revised onboarding exercise asks the analyst to resolve two deliberately similar specimen codes and explain the decision. The exercise result will show whether the instructions work for someone who did not participate in the original pilot.
items: The analyst completed the example notebook and flagged two ambiguous labels.

entry.summary:
Collected structured feedback from a rehearsal with internal reviewers. Feedback was captured against the exact chart and scenario shown during rehearsal. The team can now distinguish requests about the data story from requests about font size or controls.

The feedback sheet preserves the reviewer's words beside the team's interpretation and proposed change. This keeps a request for a clearer scenario explanation from being reduced to a cosmetic chart edit during triage.
items: Reviewers requested a shorter legend and clearer unit labels.

entry.summary:
Run a paired-sample exercise to check how crews apply the new protocol. The exercise will use a deliberately ambiguous sample record to see whether the checklist resolves it consistently. Staff will compare decisions afterward and update the wording where interpretations differ.

Crew members will also record how long each step takes and where a second person is needed. Those observations should show whether the checklist is practical during a normal visit, rather than only understandable during a desk review.
items: Observers will record deviations without interrupting the collection.

entry.summary:
Assembling a revised equipment budget for the next phase of the pilot. Several support costs depend on the number of measurement cycles rather than the initial equipment choice. The budget notes those assumptions and preserves a range instead of a single precise estimate.

The estimate separates one-time setup from recurring measurements, maintenance, and data review. It includes a low and high case for the number of cycles, with the assumptions written beside each total. Reviewers can therefore change the workload without rebuilding the budget from memory.
items: The draft separates one-time purchases from recurring service costs.

entry.summary:
Coordinating review questions with a regional planning partner.

The partner asked for a short description of the decision a reader should make from each figure. Those prompts are being used to review whether the current annotations explain the uncertainty clearly.

The partner will review a short set of captions without a presenter in the room. Their notes should reveal which assumptions are clear in the written report and which still depend on verbal explanation during the demonstration.
items: The partner will assess whether the scenario narrative is understandable.

entry.summary:
Testing a low-power relay for the remote station before outdoor installation.

Bench observations so far show stable transmission under normal load. The remaining checks focus on recovery after a power interruption and the clarity of the device status indicators.

The relay test includes a repeatable sequence of normal shutdown, abrupt power loss, and reconnection. Each run records the first valid packet after restart, battery state, and any intervention needed at the station.
items: The bench test includes intermittent connectivity and a simulated battery drop.

entry.summary:
Demonstrated the comparison dashboard during an internal review meeting.

The rehearsal showed that reviewers interpreted two colors as different confidence levels, although they represented separate sample groups. The design team is revising the legend and will test the change with another reader.

The next review will ask participants to describe what each color means before reading the legend. Their responses will be compared with the intended interpretation, and the design will be revised if the same confusion remains. The team will keep the original and revised screenshots so the decision is visible in the review record.
items: Reviewers asked for clearer legends and an explanation of uncertainty.

entry.summary:
Updated the demonstration checklist and assigned owners for open issues. Each open issue has a named owner and a check that can be completed before the room is set up. The list is intentionally short enough to use during the final rehearsal.

A final rehearsal will walk through the checklist in the room where the demonstration is planned. The team will mark each item only after its visible result is confirmed, including display contrast, exported tables, and the path back to the opening scenario.
items: The checklist includes accessibility, data provenance, and room setup.

entry.summary:
Improved the dashboard filter for stations that have not reported recently. Previously, a station under planned service could look identical to a station with an unknown failure. The revised filter makes that distinction visible in both the summary view and the export.

The change was checked with stations in three conditions: reporting normally, temporarily out of service, and missing without a known cause. The interface and downloaded table use the same labels, so a reviewer can trace what was shown on screen to the exported evidence.
items: The filter now distinguishes maintenance periods from unexplained outages.

entry.summary:
Checking whether instrument exports preserve the original sample order. Older instrument files appear to sort rows by acquisition time, while newer exports preserve submission order. The crosswalk will make that difference explicit before any merged table is released.

The acquisition order check will be repeated on files from two instrument versions. A small audit table will show the source row, normalized row, specimen label, and timestamp. If the ordering differs, the ingestion note will state which field controls the sort and why. The team will test the resulting comparison with a deliberately shuffled sample before approving the export.
items: A crosswalk table is being prepared for older files.

entry.summary:
Added an export that preserves scenario names in the downloaded table. Earlier exports omitted the comparison label and were difficult to interpret away from the interface. The revised table includes enough context for a reviewer to reproduce the displayed selection.

The exported file also records the run date, selected regions, and units used on the chart. A reviewer can compare two exports without relying on a filename chosen by the browser or a memory of the controls selected during the demonstration.
items: The export also records the selected comparison period.

entry.summary:
Finished a sensitivity check on the daily aggregation method. The comparison tested alternate minimum-coverage rules and one different treatment of short gaps. The overall pattern was consistent, while several individual peaks moved enough to merit a note in the release.

Analysts retained the alternate aggregates in a comparison file rather than replacing the original series. That record makes it possible to inspect the handful of affected peaks and decide whether a caveat or a revised rule is appropriate for the next release.
items: The main trend remained stable across the three tested thresholds.
Short-lived peaks still require manual review.

entry.summary:
Compared two baseline models on the same held-out synthetic observations. The comparison held preprocessing and evaluation splits constant so only the model choice changed. The result favors a baseline that can be explained and rerun without an additional tuning stage.

The models were also compared on error by specimen group rather than a single aggregate score. Reviewers can see whether the preferred baseline performs consistently or hides a weak subset. The team retained the evaluation split and notebook version so the comparison can be rerun after the pilot data are updated.
items: The simpler model performed comparably and is easier to explain.

entry.summary:
Auditing scenario inputs for duplicated region identifiers.

Several older input files reused a regional code after a boundary change. The audit records which interpretation was applied and flags files that cannot be resolved automatically.

The audit retains the source code and proposed normalized code in separate columns. Any unresolved case will remain outside the demonstration input set until a domain reviewer confirms the mapping, preventing an apparently clean chart from hiding a changed boundary.
items: The team is testing how the parser handles older naming conventions.

entry.summary:
Prepare a short walkthrough of the demonstration data for visiting collaborators.

The demonstration will begin with a simple station history before showing cross-site comparisons. Presenters are preparing a short explanation of synthetic values so viewers do not mistake them for operational measurements.

The walkthrough includes a small printed data key and a pause for questions after each figure. The team will capture which terms viewers ask about most often, then use that feedback to simplify the report captions before the next review.
items: The walkthrough uses synthetic observations and includes an accessibility check.

entry.summary:
Repeat the preparation trial with a second operator and a blind checklist.

The second operator will use the same materials and record timing independently. Differences will be reviewed against the checklist before the team changes any procedure.

The next trial will use the same checklist for each operator and record any deviation at the point it occurs. Those notes will help separate variation caused by the written procedure from variation introduced by instrument readiness or sample handling.
items: The trial will focus on steps that produced the largest variation.

entry.summary:
Draft a concise methods note for the simulation example. The note will show a small worked example before listing the model choices. Reviewers should be able to see which elements are illustrative without reading the full technical appendix.

The worked example will trace one synthetic disruption from initial load loss through the modeled restoration steps. A small table will list the inputs next to the generated outputs, with a note identifying assumptions chosen only to make the example readable.
items: The note will separate illustrative assumptions from measured inputs.

entry.summary:
Reviewing duplicate measurements produced during network reconnection. Two reconnection episodes produced packets with the same device time but different arrival times. The review will retain a trace of each decision so the curated series can be reproduced.

The review distinguishes identical retransmissions from packets with a changed payload. A decision table records device time, receipt time, and retained value for each case. The team will rerun the curated export after the rule is approved and compare row counts with the raw archive.
items: The team is comparing device logs with ingestion timestamps before removing records.

entry.summary:
Adding provenance fields to generated plots and exported tables. Provenance is being added where a chart is created, not as a manual annotation afterward. That approach should keep screenshots and exported tables aligned when the notebook is rerun.

Each generated file will include the input table version, notebook revision, and date of the run. A reviewer can trace a figure back to its source without relying on a manually maintained filename. The team will compare two runs with changed thresholds to confirm the provenance fields update automatically.
items: Each export will include the source run and processing version.

entry.summary:
Estimating the compute and support effort for a broader pilot. Compute demand changes with the number of scenarios and the length of each run. The estimate also includes time for reviewing results and responding to issues found during a pilot.

The pilot estimate separates simulation runtime, result review, accessibility checks, and support for the partner's questions. It includes a range for the number of scenarios and explains which costs scale with that range. This gives the planning group a way to resize the pilot without changing its review goals.
items: The estimate includes a range for review and maintenance time.

entry.summary:
Document the handoff steps for the next monthly reporting window. The handoff note will identify open data checks, equipment work, and decisions awaiting collaborators. Each item will carry a next action and date rather than only a status label.

The handoff also names the source file, last review date, and reviewer for every open item. A new reporting lead should be able to identify the next action without reconstructing it from email. The team will rehearse the handoff using an intentionally incomplete sample record and revise any step that relies on unwritten local knowledge.
items: The handoff will identify an owner for each data and equipment issue.

entry.summary:
Collect reviewer comments into a single decision log before the next planning meeting. Review comments currently arrive in several files and meeting notes. The decision log will link each request to the evidence considered and the person responsible for a follow-up.

Each comment will be marked as accepted, deferred, or awaiting evidence. For deferred comments, the log records the reason and the date for another look. The planning lead will review the longest chains of decisions with the team so earlier context is still available when an issue returns.

For each decision, the log will retain the source comment, the response discussed at the meeting, and the evidence that supports it. Reviewers will be able to see when two comments refer to the same issue and when an apparently similar request needs a separate answer. Before the next draft is circulated, the team will verify that accepted changes appear in the figures, captions, and companion data table.
items: The log will distinguish accepted changes from items needing evidence.

entry.summary:
Trained a second reviewer to run the accessibility checklist.

The second reviewer found a label that sounded clear in the checklist but was difficult to locate on the chart. The item has been rewritten to point to the visible control and its expected behavior.

The training record includes the reviewer's independent findings and the final disposition for each issue. It will be used to refine the checklist where two reviewers interpret a control differently, especially when the difference affects a keyboard user.
items: Both reviewers used the same synthetic scenarios for comparison.

entry.summary: Prepare a common accessibility checklist for report figures and presentation materials. The first draft will be tested on a figure, a table, and a short presentation. Reviewers will note where a requirement is hard to apply so the guidance stays practical.
items: The checklist will cover contrast, text alternatives, and readable labels.

entry.summary: Established a monthly cross-project review to surface shared dependencies and upcoming demonstrations. The review will focus on dependencies that cross project boundaries and on decisions that need a common owner. Routine project details will remain in their individual sections.
items: Project teams will provide short written updates before each review.

entry.summary:
Run an observation session to test how readers interpret uncertainty bands. Participants will explain what they think each band means before seeing the legend. The team will use those observations to revise labels rather than assuming more explanatory text is sufficient.

The observation guide avoids explaining the intended answer before participants respond. Facilitators will record the participant's reading of the bands, the legend terms they consult, and any question asked after the scenario changes. The team will compare observations across readers before rewriting the figure caption, then repeat the test with the revised wording.
items: The session will capture points of confusion before the design is finalized.

entry.summary:
Finished a stress test with delayed restoration in multiple regions. The stress test used the same synthetic demand traces as the baseline and changed only the restoration timing. The ambiguous label is being revised before the result is reused in a presentation.

The team retained the baseline and delayed-restoration outputs with identical plot scales and region order. Reviewers can therefore focus on the timing change without mentally normalizing two different charts. A separate note lists which conclusions hold across both runs and which depend on the stress-test assumption. Before release, another analyst will reproduce the figures from the stored inputs and check that every caption names the correct scenario.

The example also includes a deliberately dense explanation of the most uncertain case. It describes the input perturbation, the constraints applied to restoration, and the checks used to separate a model response from a plotting error. The final review will decide which uncertainty caveats must accompany the chart when it is shared outside the project team.
items: The test exposed a chart label that becomes ambiguous at long durations.

entry.summary: Ordered replacement compute hardware and confirmed a datacenter location for the shared test environment. The shared environment supports the synthetic demonstrations used throughout this report. The team is documenting dependencies before equipment arrives so installation decisions can be reviewed together.
items: A kickoff with the vendor is planned for the next reporting period.
The installation plan includes a network and power review.
